subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: `computeFitScale` returns one scalar, `min((w-2padX)/designW, (h-2padY)/designH)`. It is clamped to MIN_SCALE and the mode's maxScale. `useFitScale` feeds it the stage box's own `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` through a `ResizeObserver` on that box, not the window, so it fits the area the stage occupies. Stage applies it as `scale(${scale})` on both axes to a fixed-size canvas. At 390 wide the scale is about 0.37–0.41, well above the 0.2 floor, so the canvas fits. At 1280×720 the scale is about 1.1–1.3, below the 1.5/3 caps, so it is fit-limited.

criteria.rationale: I traced each of the five templates in templates/presentation against the bootstrap kit and tsconfig. No test materializes and builds the `new` templates, so this rests on the trace. The skill materializes them into src/presentations/<slug>/. From there, `../../presentation-kit/index.ts` resolves to src/presentation-kit/index.ts, inside src. scaffold.mjs `newPresentation` also rewrites that import to the project's actual kit entry, so non-default layouts still resolve. `./styles.css` and `./Scene.tsx`, `./steps.ts` and `./entities.ts` are all siblings that the same command writes. Every symbol the templates import is exported by the kit's index.ts: Presentation, defineStep, Appear, Arrow, Box, SceneLayer, SymbolChip and the SceneProps type. Required props and field names match the kit's types. Talk.tsx passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`, and PresentationProps requires only `steps` and `title`. Each `defineStep` call supplies id, era, title, caption, Scene, groupKey and payload. That matches Step<TPayload>, whose StepMeta fields are id, era, title and caption. Box and SymbolChip get the required `id`, with `at` as a Rect. Arrow gets `id`, `from` and `to` from G.link. Appear and SceneLayer take children and the `key` prop. Under the strict tsconfig.app.json settings (noUnusedLocals, verbatimModuleSyntax, allowImportingTsExtensions), every import in the templates is used, and type-only imports use inline `type`.

engineering-quality.rationale: All four script copies reach `preview.stop()` from a finally block, and the preview is spawned directly as `node vite.js` with a process-group SIGTERM. But `stop()` only sends the signal and returns nothing. Nothing awaits the child's exit, and the 'exit' handler only sets a flag. The requirement is to terminate and await the preview server process, so the await clause is unmet. In inspect, `mkdirSync` also runs after `startPreview()` and outside the try, so a throw there would leave the preview running.
evidence: scripts/lib.mjs startPreview: `stop` calls process.kill(-child.pid,'SIGTERM') and returns; `cleanup` calls stop() and deletes itself from `cleanups`; no promise waits on the child's '…
scripts/verify.mjs and scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs: `finally { await browser?.close(); preview.stop() }` with stop() not awaited.
The bootstrap lib.mjs, verify.mjs and inspect-presentation.mjs copies are the same.

engineering-quality.rationale: Readiness polls over HTTP in a loop capped at 100 iterations. Each fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(1000)`, and the loop ends in a CheckError. Verify and inspect both await `run('npm',['run','build'])` before `startPreview()`. Readiness does not parse printed output, so the ANSI and chunk-splitting clause does not apply. The other waits (`waitForSelector`, `waitForFunction`) have explicit timeouts.
evidence: lib.mjs startPreview: `for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++)` with `fetch(..., { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1000) })` and `sleep(100)`, then throws 'did not become ready'.
verify.mjs verify(): `await run('npm',['run','build'],'build')` precedes `await startPreview()`.
inspect-presentation.mjs: build is awaited when opts.build is true, before startPreview().

votes.rationale: `computeFitScale` returns one scalar, `min((w-2padX)/designW, (h-2padY)/designH)`. It is clamped to MIN_SCALE and the mode's maxScale. `useFitScale` feeds it the stage box's own `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` through a `ResizeObserver` on that box, not the window, so it fits the area the stage occupies. Stage applies it as `scale(${scale})` on both axes to a fixed-size canvas. At 390 wide the scale is about 0.37–0.41, well above the 0.2 floor, so the canvas fits. At 1280×720 the scale is about 1.1–1.3, below the 1.5/3 caps, so it is fit-limited.

votes.rationale: startPreview reserves an ephemeral port with freePort(), closes that listener, and starts the preview with --strictPort. Readiness is taken only from HTTP polling: `fetch(base/)` returning ok. The only ownership check is the `exited` flag, tested at the top of each loop iteration before the request. The child's own announcement is never used, and readiness is not raced against the child's exit. If another process takes the released port, it can answer the probe with HTTP 200 before the child's exit is observed, so verification would run against a server it does not own. The guidance names this pattern as a fail, and says a strict port alone is insufficient.

votes.rationale: Neither credited ownership mechanism is present. Readiness comes from HTTP-polling the URL with fetch, not from the child's own announcement of its address. The child's exit is checked only through an `exited` flag sampled at the top of each loop iteration, before the fetch, and it is not raced against the poll. The port is freshly reserved and `--strictPort` is set, but the port is closed after reservation and before spawn. audit_results.rationale: The quoted lines satisfy every clause. (1) Unreadable step count: verify.mjs:35-36 applies Number() to data-step-count and throws CheckError('render') when !(count > 0). Missing (Number(null)=0), zero and non-numeric (NaN) values all fail before any stepping, so verification cannot pass while stepping through no steps. (2) Transition comparison: verify.mjs:44-50 compares the raw data-step-index attribute string with String(i) under strict equality. An absent hook (null) or a non-numeric one never satisfies the comparison, and no Number(null) === 0 coercion exists. Step 1 involves no transition, so nothing there is counted as progress. (3) Failure reporting and exit: lines 118-123 print `FAIL phase=render step=N` and set process.exitCode = 1. (4) Focused test: verify.test.ts:71-75 breaks next() so the transition never advances, runs scripts/verify.mjs, and asserts a non-zero exit and /FAIL phase=render step=2: .*transition did not advance/. That is a step that fails to advance, with both the exit and the offending step asserted.

presentation-skill.rationale: The auditor's facts are accurate. scaffold() copies filesFor('index'), which includes everything under src/presentations/. The registry registers getting-started, and that presentation's styles.css sets colors, system-ui fonts, borders and backgrounds. But this does not defeat the pass on this criterion. The scenario this criterion tests asks for a full scaffold of build setup, scene kit and presentation index, with the required dependencies installed, before the presentation is created. Its review guidance lists exactly what to check: the template holds all three anchors and the dependency set; SKILL.md directs a full scaffold and an install; a test materializes the template in a fresh location and builds it; the scene-kit snapshot matches the canonical kit; and Chromium is installed or checked for. Style neutrality is not on that list. The contract scores it under its own criterion, skill-scaffold-style-neutral, whose guidance is to inspect the template's dependencies and styles. The styling the auditor cites also sits in a file owned by the presentation, which the fixture allows for presentation styling. The scene kit and src/index.css stay free of visual defaults. So even if this clause counted against skill-scaffold-style-neutral, it would not make this criterion's scenario unmet. A fact the requirement does not depend on cannot turn this pass into a fail.

engineering-quality.rationale: The material does show that the arrow test calls startPreview() and launchBrowser() before its try/finally, so a Chromium launch failure would skip the test's preview.stop(). But this criterion's guidance says 'a missing browser installation is not scored here', and that is exactly the case where launchBrowser throws. The guidance names only two fail cases: a shared hardcoded port, and killing only the npx wrapper. The rules forbid failing on a scenario the guidance doesn't name. On every path the test actually produces, it stops the real Vite process (spawned directly through process.execPath and killed by process group) and closes the browser in finally. Ports are dynamic. So the pass verdict stands.
evidence: bootstrap.test.ts arrow test: `const preview = await startPreview(); const browser = await launchBrowser(); try { ... } finally { await browser.close(); preview.stop() }`.
lib.mjs launchBrowser throws CheckError('browser', 'could not launch Chromium ...') only when the Chromium launch fails, which is the missing-browser case the guidance excludes ('…
lib.mjs startPreview spawns `process.execPath vite.js preview` detached and stops it with process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGTERM'). This kills the real server, not an npm/npx wrapper.
lib.mjs freePort uses server.listen(0, HOST), so preview ports are allocated dynamically.
verify.test.ts checks with pgrep that no vite.js process remains after each fault run, including the browser launch failure run.

If `process.kill(-child.pid)` fails (e.g. the group is gone), it falls back to `child.kill`. This is fine, but `process.exit(130)` in `onSignal` runs while verify's `finally` (browser.close) never executes, which leaks the Chromium process on Ctrl-C.
  ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib.mjs:81 The readiness probe `fetch(`${base}/`)` has no timeout.
